outcome: poor wound healing after forceps delivery
cohort: The study included 148 patients who underwent forceps delivery, with 74 patients experiencing poor wound healing and 74 patients having normal wound healing.
finding: Labor length, anemia after delivery, postpartum fever, and degree of laceration were identified as risk factors for poor perineal wound healing after forceps delivery, while postpartum antibiotics and prolonged suture removal days were protective factors.
mod_finding: The study identified several risk factors (labor length, degree of laceration) and protective factors (postpartum antibiotics, suture removal days) specifically impacting perineal wound healing following forceps delivery.
birth_weight: Not specified for the entire cohort, but patients with poor wound healing had a larger birthweight.
